key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 steel, giving the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve oxidation protection for SA516 boiler steel exposed to high temperatures.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The reported 95.71% reduction in weight gain accompanied protective oxide formation, while bare steel showed intense oxide-layer spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated under laboratory air oxidation; durability in actual boiler combustion environments remains to be established.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
